title: Whole-genome CRISPR screening identifies N-glycosylation as a genetic and therapeutic vulnerability in CALR-mutant MPNs
model: BA/F3-MPL cells (empty vector or CALR del52), mouse Brie genome-wide knockout library
contrast: CALR del52 without IL3 vs empty vector with IL3, day 21 (2 vs 2 independent lines)
paper_calls: 669 genes with log2FC < -1 (23 at MAGeCK FDR 0.05); 7 of the top 10 in protein glycosylation, Dpm2 most depleted
barcs_calls: 24 genes at FDR 0.10 (16 depleted, 8 enriched); 49 against the control null
named_hits: 3/5 at FDR 0.10 (Dpm2 #1, Dpm3 #2, Dpm1 #6); Calr #19 and Mpdu1 #20 at FDR 0.13-0.14
verdict: BARCS reproduces the N-glycosylation dependency (Dpm1/2/3, Mpi, Pmm2, Dpy19l1, Uggt1, Srd5a3) and 15 of its 16 depleted calls are MAGeCK FDR 0.10 genes; Calr and Mpdu1 just miss because one of four guides is flat with only two lines per arm.
